commenti.body:
>Did DeNiro pluck him out of obscurity for "A Bronx Tale"

You know "A Bronx Tale" was a one man play written and performed by Palminteri, and he wrote the screenplay for the movie right?
Yeah but deniro made it happen on film.
Also - his name is actually Calogero

A bit harsh? - Just a question - maybe it’s just me. - These rising star references - movies Chaz got and why - were quite some time ago, right?  So, I may be the only person who replies here. Anyway - Young Chaz worked hard - acted, wrote, developed his one man show in a small LA theatre. It came to DeNiro’s attention at a time the icon was looking to direct. Stars aligned for the unknown actor/writer - who wrote and performed in a killer Equity Waiver show - and then he grabbed the gold ring. Chaz then capitalized on that bright moment and built it, through the next years, based on talent, charisma and solid management/representation decisions. His “ushering in” (as you call it) was never “weird” - IMHO - when you compare it to at any other “hot new character actor”in Hollywood. - It was a a steady progression with a lot of excellent contacts, career savvy, talent, and timing. - You may not like watching  Chaz onscreen but that’s just a “taster’s choice” thing. His career arc is one that any newbie might investigate, understand and, if possible, emulate. Work hard - have talent - produce a product that professionals outside your current league respond to - at all times, have a realistic understanding of your place in the Hollywood eco system (humility) - listen - listen - listen - and then be ready when the next stepping stone is offered. Chaz exceeded at this and built a commendable career. Like his face- don’t like his face meh. Talent rises to the top.
